edits.old: With read concern `linearizable`, reads on the primary return data reflecting successful majority-acknowledged writes completed before the read begins and may wait for concurrent writes to propagate to a majority. MongoDB does not support this level in transactions or causally consistent sessions. The guarantee applies only when the query filter uniquely identifies one document. A consistent snapshot is not assured unless the search key is immutable, no concurrent update mutates that key, or the query uses a unique index on the search key. MongoDB recommends `maxTimeMS` to bound waits when a majority of data-bearing members are unavailable; Percona's MongoDB 3.4 review describes the same before-read guarantee. (high confidence)
